Commentary.Commentary: We are back for Sri Lanka's batting effort. The two umpires and players have made their way out to the middle. It will be Pathum Nissanka and Kusal Mendis to open the innings for Sri Lanka. Khaleel Ahmed will start with the new ball for India. Away we go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, the game is nicely poised at the halfway mark. Sri Lanka bowled 14 overs of spin, which tells you everything you need to know about how the wicket is behaving. The Indian spinners will be licking their lips at the prospect of bowling on this surface, which is offering sharp turn and bounce. Sri Lanka have a tricky total to overhaul and a good Powerplay will be crucial to their chances in the chase. Join us back in a bit for what should be an interesting chase.

As for Sri Lanka, the debutant, Chamindu Wickramasinghe and Maheesh Theekshana set things up nicely for them. Asitha Fernando too chipped in the Powerplay to put India on the back foot. The middle phase saw India make a comeback as overs 7-15 went for 67 runs at the loss of just one wicket. With a double strike through Wanindu Hasaranga, dismissing both set batters in a single over, Sri Lanka were able to reclaim the ascendancy in the game back. With Matheesha Pathirana feeling his right shoulder due to an effort in the field, Charith Asalanka did not have the option to go to his strike bowler but the rest did well to fill the void.

After being asked to bat first, India were off to a shaky start. Losing four wickets in the Powerplay, the visitors found themselves right behind the eight ball. India's top order was blown away in a flash on a challenging surface but Gill held onto his end. He saw the procession of wickets from the other end as India's score read 48/5 just before the 9th over. Shubman Gill and Riyan Parag then got together and kept the scoreboard ticking with ones and twos. Just as the two batters were beginning to put their foot on the gas, losing both in the same over pegged India back. Sundar's 18-ball 25 ensured that India took some value from the back end of the innings and got close to 140.

A good couple of balls, more importantly, dots, for Sri Lanka to keep India under 140! India, though, will not be too disappointed with what they have ended up with. From 48/5, the visitors added 89 runs for the loss of 4 wickets to finish with 137 on the board

OUT! RUN OUT! A good finish for Sri Lanka overall. Quick, flat and short outside off, Mohammed Siraj throws his bat it at to slash it away, but misses on the outside edge. Kusal Mendis initially fails to collect it cleanly behind the stumps and the ball drops near the strip. Seizing this opportunity, Siraj and Bishnoi look to cross for a single. Kusal Mendis however, is quick to make amends and is quickly reacts to his error to redeem himself. He picks the ball moving forward and scores a direct hit to the non-striker's end. Siraj is way outside the crease when the ball breaks into the stumps. India finish at 137/9.

Commentary.Commentary: Shade fuller in length, outside off, Shubman Gill pats it through the off side for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.1: Chamindu Wickramasinghe to Shubman Gill, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Short of a good length, at the stumps, Shivam Dube punches it to mid off. End of the mandatory Powerplay, India are reeling at the moment - 30/4 with the top order blown away very quickly.

OUT! IN THE AIR AND TAKEN! SKY falls too! India in a deep trouble here! Asitha Fernando hurls it on a fuller length, in front of the stumps, Suryakumar Yadav sits on his knee and goes for his favourite lap shot to deposit the ball behind the square but doesn't quite get the timing correct and airs it straight towards Wanindu Hasaranga patrolling the deep backward square leg region. He takes a regulation catch and Sri Lanka are right on the top here. Asitha Fernando is elated and all pumped up and why not? Suryakumar Yadav departs on 8 (9). Sometimes your strength becomes your weakness!
Commentary.Howout: c Wanindu Hasaranga b Asitha Fernando
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.4: Asitha Fernando to Suryakumar Yadav, OUT! c Wanindu Hasaranga b Asitha Fernando.

Commentary.Commentary: Hard length angling on the middle and leg, Shubman Gill respects the ball and taps it in front of mid on and quickly gets to the other end.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.3: Asitha Fernando to Shubman Gill, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: This one jags back in, hard length angling on the off stump line, Suryakumar Yadav dabs it off the back foot to short third and rotates the strike.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.2: Asitha Fernando to Suryakumar Yadav, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Asitha starts his spell from over the stumps, delivers it on a fullish length with the ball shaping away outside off, Suryakumar Yadav covers his stumps and goes to swipe it across the line to access his productive area behind the square on the leg side. He gets beaten by the movement.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.1: Asitha Fernando to Suryakumar Yadav, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Change? Will Theekshana too, get his third over? No, he won't. Asitha Fernando has been introduced into the attack now.
Beaten! Shaping into the right-hander, on a length, outside off, Shubman Gill gives himself room to slap it past point but gets beaten on the inside edge as the ball nips back in.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.6: Chamindu Wickramasinghe to Shubman Gill, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Easy pickings! Wickramasinghe errs in line and length as he bowls it too full and on the pads. Shubman Gill gets inside the line and glances it to the left of short fine leg for his first boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.5: Chamindu Wickramasinghe to Shubman Gill, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: In the air...but it just about evades mid on! Wickramasinghe bowls it full and straight, at the stumps. Shubman Gill charges down the track and looks to go over mid off. The bat turns in his hand but Gill gets enough back on it to clear Charith Asalanka there who turns around and goes after it. Two runs taken.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.4: Chamindu Wickramasinghe to Shubman Gill, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Full and sliding on the pads, flicked down to deep fine leg for a single by Suryakumar Yadav.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.3: Chamindu Wickramasinghe to Suryakumar Yadav, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Full and on off. Suryakumar Yadav defends it right under his eyeline.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.2: Chamindu Wickramasinghe to Suryakumar Yadav, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: In the corridor on off and Wickramasinghe is still getting the away shape, fuller and outside off. Suryakumar Yadav leaves the ball alone.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.1: Chamindu Wickramasinghe to Suryakumar Yadav, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Change? Nope, Chamindu Wickramasinghe (2-0-5-1) is back to deliver his third over.
This keeps a bit low on the shorter side by Theekshana, on off. Shubman Gill stays low and punches it to cover.

Commentary.Commentary: Attacks the stumps, on a nagging length, Suryakumar Yadav wrists this one past mid on and rotates the strike.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! In the gap! Maheesh Theekshana goes full and on the middle and leg, Suryakumar Yadav reads the ball well from the release and flicks it nicely through the gap between the mid on and mid-wicket region for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.4: Maheesh Theekshana to Suryakumar Yadav, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Flatter and shorter, on middle, Shubman Gill nudges it past square leg and gets to the other end.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.3: Maheesh Theekshana to Shubman Gill, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Tossed up by Theekshana, full and on off, Suryakumar Yadav gets on the front foot and knocks it to long on for a single to open his account.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.2: Maheesh Theekshana to Suryakumar Yadav, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: It has just not been easy to play big strokes from the outset here. And to be fair, both Lankan bowlers have come out prepared and are bowling according to the condition demands. A procession of wickets early on for India. 3 down now. Who walks in next to bat? The Indian skipper Suryakumar Yadav strides out at number 5.

OUT! TAKEN! The start gets better for Sri Lanka ​​​Maheesh Theekshana strikes again! Theekshana gets rewarded for his bravery as he loops it up and entices the batter into the big shot. Full and outside off. Rinku Singh ends up giving himself too much room to go over the off side. Rinku is early into his shot and spoons it up off the bottom half of the bat and it goes only as far as mid off where Matheesha Pathirana runs to his left from long on, keeps his eyes on the ball and takes it near his chest. India have been rocked early. They are 14/3 after 3.1 overs.
Commentary.Howout: c Matheesha Pathirana b Maheesh Theekshana
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.1: Maheesh Theekshana to Rinku Singh, OUT! c Matheesha Pathirana b Maheesh Theekshana.

Commentary.Commentary: WIDE! Fired down leg by Maheesh Theekshana for a wide.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.1: Maheesh Theekshana to Rinku Singh, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: Good stop! Bowled full by Wickramasinghe, on off, Rinku Singh drives it firmly towards cover where Pathum Nissanka dives to his left to take the sting out of the ball. Just a single taken.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.6: Chamindu Wickramasinghe to Rinku Singh, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Another duck for Sanju Samson. Who walks in next? Rinku Singh walks in at number 4.

OUT! IN THE AIR AND GONE! MAIDEN INTERNATIONAL WICKET for Wickramasinghe! Look at the delight on the face of the debutant. Wickramasinghe bowls it full and this is on the off-stump line. Sanju Samson sees the delivery right in his slot but opts for the wrong option as he goes across the line. Gets a top edge that skies high in the air to the only fielder in the deep on the off side at deep backward point. Wanindu Hasaranga runs in off the ropes and dives forward to complete the catch. One more disappointing outing for Sanju Samson with bat.
Commentary.Howout: c Wanindu Hasaranga b Chamindu Wickramasinghe

Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.4: Chamindu Wickramasinghe to Sanju Samson, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Oh, that could have gone anywhere! Wickramasinghe bashes the hard length, on off. the ball lifts off the deck and Sanju Samson is through his shot early as he looks to play it straight. Chips it on the leg side but it falls safely in the vacant short mid-wicket region.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.3: Chamindu Wickramasinghe to Sanju Samson, No run.

Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.1: Chamindu Wickramasinghe to Shubman Gill, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: The ploy to bring in the spinner early on has worked for Sri Lanka as Theekshana sends the dangerous Jaiswal inside the first six. Who walks in next to bat? Opened in the 2nd T20I, Sanju Samson is back in his familiar role this time. He is in at number 3.

OUT! LBW! A loud shout for LBW and up goes the finger! This looks dead straight but Yashasvi Jaiswal after a chat with Gill, takes the review. This was tossed up by Theekshana, full and on middle from around the wicket, Yashasvi Jaiswal reached out in front to play the sweep but got beaten in the flight and missed a straight delivery. Gets pinged near the knee roll on the front pad and the dreaded finger is raised. There is nothing on UltraEdge and the Ball Tracking shows three reds with the ball crashing into the middle stump. Theekshana has the last laugh! Yashasvi Jaiswal departs on 10 (9).
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.6: Maheesh Theekshana to Yashasvi Jaiswal, OUT! lbw b Maheesh Theekshana.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Not in complete control but Yashasvi Jaiswal manages to get it away for a boundary. Theekshana pushes it through, fuller and quicker, on middle, Yashasvi Jaiswal swings too hard and loses his shape as he looks to go over mid on. Gets it off the inner half of the bat and hits it a bit uppishly but it evades mid on to his left for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.5: Maheesh Theekshana to Yashasvi Jaiswal, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: This is bowled with a flatter trajectory by Theekshana, on middle and leg, Yashasvi Jaiswal knocks it to mid on without much timing.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.4: Maheesh Theekshana to Yashasvi Jaiswal, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: The ball has held its shape a bit and it will be interesting to see how the Indian batters approach the movement in the field restrictions. Who bowls the second over? Spin from the other end. Maheesh Theekshana to share the attack.

Half a shout for LBW but that was heading down leg! Wickramasinghe angles it in, on a good length, on the pads, Shubman Gill gets on his toes but misses the flick shot. Wears it high on the front pad. A tidy start to international cricket for Wickramasinghe.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Chamindu Wickramasinghe to Shubman Gill, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Just around the off stump, on a short of a good length, Yashasvi Jaiswal frees his arms and dabs it down to deep backward point for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Chamindu Wickramasinghe to Yashasvi Jaiswal, 1 run.

Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Chamindu Wickramasinghe to Shubman Gill, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Wickramasinghe beats the bat now! Goes full and gets a good away shape, outside off. Shubman Gill is lured into the drive and makes the mistake of playing away from his body. It does not cost Gill as the ball zips past the outside edge.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.3: Chamindu Wickramasinghe to Shubman Gill, No run.

The ball rolls past mid-wicket for a single.

Commentary.Commentary: Well then, all set for the 3rd and the final T20I to commence! The two umpires are out in the middle. Sri Lankan players spread out to their respective field positions after a huddle talk near the ropes. For India, Shubman Gill who missed out on the second match due to a neck spasm walks out with his partner Yashasvi Jaiswal. And Chamindu Wickramasinghe, the 21-year-old right arm seamer, on his T20I debut is straightaway gearing up to bowl the first over. Here we go...

India (Playing XI) - Shubman Gill (In for Rishabh Pant), Yashasvi Jaiswal, Suryakumar Yadav (C), Sanju Samson (WK), Riyan Parag, Shivam Dube (In for Hardik Pandya), Rinku Singh, Washington Sundar (In for Axar Patel), Ravi Bishnoi, Khaleel Ahmed (In for Arshdeep Singh), Mohammed Siraj.

Sri Lanka (Playing XI) - Pathum Nissanka, Kusal Mendis (WK), Kusal Perera, Kamindu Mendis, Charith Asalanka (C), Chamindu Wickramasinghe (On T20I debut) (In for Dasun Shanaka), Wanindu Hasaranga, Ramesh Mendis, Maheesh Theekshana, Matheesha Pathirana, Asitha Fernando.

The skipper of India, Suryakumar Yadav says that with the weather around and it being difficult to bowl with the wet ball, they wanted to bowl first. Informs that Hardik Pandya, Arshdeep Singh, Axar Patel and Rishabh Pant have been rested. Tells that they spoke about the brand of cricket they want to play and it is about topping it up every game and being the best version of oneself.

Charith Asalanka, the captain of Sri Lanka says the pitch looks very dry so bowling is a good option. On being asked about their batting collapses, he mentions once the ball gets older it is tough to bat. Adds that they have prepared a bit differently for this game. Informs that they have made one change - Chamindu Wickramasinghe will debut and he is in for Dasun Shanaka.
TOSS - The flip of the coin lands in the favour of Charith Asalanka. Sri Lanka have opted to BOWL first.

JUST IN - Sri Lanka have announced their ODI squad for the upcoming three-match series against India, which begins on Friday, August 2. Charith Asalanka has been appointed as the new ODI captain, succeeding Kusal Mendis. Asalanka, who took over the T20I captaincy from Wanindu Hasaranga, will now lead the team in the ODI format as well.

PITCH REPORT - Russel Arnold is near the deck. He starts by saying that it is tough to predict the weather but the ground staff are hopeful that the strong winds will blow the clouds away. Adds that there might be intermittent showers but it should remain dry till 10-10:30 pm local time (the game will start at 8 pm local time). Russel informs that a fresh surface will be used for this game. Further says that this wicket is a lot drier and it looks very rough. Opines that the ball will grip but the wicket will be on the slower side. Reckons that the pacers will be effective with their slower deliveries. Feels that the captain winning the toss will look to bowl first with the possibility of a shortened game and dew. Tells that 160-170 will be a good score batting first. Says that the slower you bowl, the harder it will be for the batters to hit.

In hockey, India returned to winning ways after yesterday's 1-1 draw against Argentina, securing a 2-0 victory over Ireland. Setpieces proved decisive, with captain Harmanpreet Singh finding the back of the net twice, once via a stroke and once from a penalty corner. India will lean on this confidence as they prepare to take on stronger teams in Belgium and Australia next.

While we wait for the action to commence, let's get you up to speed with the Olympics action. From an Indian standpoint, it has been an eventful Day 4 at the Paris 2024 Olympics so far. The day began brightly with Manu Bhaker and Sarabjot Singh securing a bronze medal in the 10m air pistol mixed team event, marking India's second medal of the Games. This follows Bhaker’s earlier success two days ago, where she opened India's account in Paris with a bronze medal in the individual 10m air pistol event. By doing so, Bhaker became the first Indian female athlete to win two medals in a single edition of the Olympics. Quite an achievement for the 22-year-old shooting sensation!

For those worried about the weather, rain has been a frequent visitor in Kandy over the past couple of days. However, the forecast looks promising for the match hours, so we should be in for a good game without weather interruptions. Stay tuned for the toss and team news.

India's new T20I era, under head coach Gautam Gambhir and captain Suryakumar Yadav, has kicked off on a positive note. In both games, the visitors found themselves on the back foot, but the bowling unit bailed them out, staging impressive comebacks. Suryakumar Yadav, true to his word at the toss in the first game, has delivered on his promise of a fearless brand of cricket. With the T20I series secured and only a two-day gap before the ODI series, India might seize this opportunity to give bench players valuable game time while resting those likely to feature in the ODI series.

After the T20 World Cup debacle, Sri Lanka entered this series with hopes of turning over a new leaf. However, their mission has faltered with twin losses, and more than the defeats themselves, it is the manner of these losses that will sting for Charith Asalanka and his team. Sri Lanka’s series has been marred by twin collapses, where they have squandered strong positions in both matches. Despite solid performances from their top order, led by Pathum Nissanka, the middle order has failed to deliver, resulting in frustrating and costly batting collapses.

Hello and a warm welcome, folks, to our coverage of the third and final T20I between Sri Lanka and India. We are at the Pallekele International Cricket Stadium in Kandy for one final time on India's tour of the island nation before the caravan will shift to Colombo for the ODI series. With India holding an unassailable 2-0 lead, they’ll be aiming for a clean sweep, while Sri Lanka will be looking to salvage some pride and make their mark on the series.
... MATCH DAY ...

The third and final T20I of the series between Sri Lanka and India awaits us at the Pallekele International Cricket Stadium in Kandy. With India holding a 2-0 lead, there is no way back for Sri Lanka in the series but will aim to finish on a high note and carry momentum into the ODI series. The story for Sri Lanka has been marked by twin collapses, resulting in them squandering strong positions in both matches. In the series opener, they crumbled from 140/1 to 170 all out. In the second game, they were 130/2 at the end of 15 overs but lost 7 wickets for just 31 runs, finishing with only 161. It did not get any better from them as India made light work of the revised target of 78 runs in 8 overs. Sri Lanka’s top order has performed well, but their middle order has faltered. Charith Asalanka must lead the charge, and Kamindu Mendis, who showed promise in the last game, must also step up. All-rounders Dasun Shanaka and Wanindu Hasaranga have not had much impact and will need to improve their performances. Matheesha Pathirana has been the standout bowler for Sri Lanka, but he needs more support from Maheesh Theekshana and Asitha Fernando to avoid a clean sweep. On the other hand, India’s new era in T20Is, with Gautam Gambhir as head coach and Suryakumar Yadav as full-time captain, has begun just as they would have hoped. In both games, their bowling was put to the test, but once they found an opening, they barged through. Spin twins Ravi Bishnoi and Axar Patel have been particularly effective for the visitors. Arshdeep Singh has been consistently reliable, but his new ball partner, Mohammed Siraj, has blown hot and cold. Yashasvi Jaiswal and Suryakumar Yadav have exemplified the aggressive brand of cricket India aim to play. Shubman Gill, who missed the last game due to a neck spasm, might return to the lineup, potentially replacing Sanju Samson. With the series already won, India may make additional changes to give bench players some game time. Will India complete the clean sweep? Or will Sri Lanka find the resilience to bounce back and salvage some pride? We shall find out soon enough.
